item.title: Re: I'd Rather Be Part of the Serpent's Hand Than the Foundation"
item.content:encoded:
No locked door can ever be justified, no matter what lies on the other side. No cage can be justified, no matter what it holds back. Knowledge is free for anyone regardless of intent, except to those deemed unworthy- especially those who question any of the previous.

As I said before: S.H. isn't going around breaching highly dangerous euclids and keters just for the sake of it. They aren't stupid, and they don't want the end of the world. They just want knowledge of the paranormal to be out in the open and accessible, and also want equal rights for anomalous humans (especially reality benders). The Serpent's Hand does believe in the destruction or containment of highly dangerous anomalies, however. Also, the Serpent's Hand is not without their flaws, either. You are acting as if the Foundation has no flaws, as well.

Also, the SH deems everybody worthy of knowledge of the occult, so long as they use that knowledge for good.

The Foundation is an organization of mortals … They have no illusions about their own ethics- They know that sometimes the right call is the lesser of two evils, and accept the consequences of that.

Are you sure? I find locking people up simply because they are abnormal is pretty evil. Some of the anomalous humans in Foundation containment haven't even done anything wrong.


Forum category: SCP Universe / Foundation Universe
Forum thread: I'd Rather Be Part of the Serpent's Hand Than the Foundation"

OK, so for this one, here's short reasons for why I've downvoted.

First of all, I want to be clear that I don't think your article is bad by any means. You've clearly done work about that, the grammar is perfect and the way you write it is pretty good, I've not really seem something that looked non-clinical or something like that.

But there's two reasons of why I downvote. The first one is the fact that, when I've readed some paragraphs, I've thought at least two times "Wait a minute, that looks like a SCPDeclassified post who weirdly tries to take an in-universe approach" and it felt off-topic at times (Wizz talked about the fact that in the article, 173 is a famous thing and it feels weird).

And the second reason is that, even if it's clear that you've done work and research, the paragraphs and the way it's organized looks like big walls of text, to the point that I had struggle reading that because there was too much words and too much scientific things implied, I was a bit lost.

So, that's why I downvote. But I can see a great lot of potential on your Tale, so I highly suggest you to rework it and pay attention to what others suggested you to do.

item.title: The Recursive Dollhouse
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Fridge Horror/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: Essentially, SCP-XXXX a dollhouse of whatever environment it is currently being contained within. Likewise, it would sustain a diminished capability of whatever building it is housed in. SCP-XXXX-1 are essentially "dolls" housed in the facility that make up sentient/concious organisms. This also applies to anomalous materials as well, such as me, the toaster that speaks in the first person or the mask SCP. In addition, the anomalous effects of objects are still maintained but to a much smaller degree. Objects within the SCP-XXXX move in tandem with their current reality counterparts. Actions made within the main facility are mirrored in SCP-XXXX. There is in fact a miniature version of SCP-XXXX (dubbed SCP-XXXXa) and it is theorized that there are multiple versions of SCP-XXXX that exist within the dimensional realm.

Central Narrative: The SCP Foundation found this dollhouse in the middle of a nursery amongst other toys. After examining this, an entity attempts to contact them (potentially, though I am not sold on the concept) in an attempt to get it back.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The inherent dread of a recursive universe where what we view from within could in fact be caused by an upper plane of existence is terrifying, no?

Additional Notes: Edit 1: As for what happens when objects or instances of SCP-XXXX-1 are affected by outside users, I'd like to go into that further within test logs potentially. If not, essentially, the-what I dub-"dollhouse reality" can be affected by users. The current reality would be marginally affected in a similar manner. This isn't compulsory, however, but it does bring about satisfaction of the affected individual to complete said task. Other more violent actions such as the destruction of an instance of SCP-XXXX-1 can cause a severely minimized effect on the affected individual.If an anomalous SCP-XXXX-1 instance comes in contact with a non-anomalous instance of SCP-XXXX-1, the effects that would be generated by the anomalous instance are greatly minimized. Objects brought into the SCP-XXXX reality will manifest in the current reality as well.

item.title: Re: Real Life Publishing Opportunities
item.content:encoded:
Some people expressed interest in me making posts more, so:

Mermaids Monthly is a kickstarter that has a submissions window opening up.

The first submission period for Mermaids Monthly will open on the 20th of December 2020 and close on the 9th of January, 2021.

What kinds of things can I submit?

Fiction up to 5,000 words. There is no minimum word count, and we love flash! (we pay $0.10/word for fiction)

Poetry of any length (we pay $50 – $100 for poems)

Comics up to 5 pages (we pay $75-$100 per page)

Each to Each micro art and word submissions (more below—we pay $25 for these)

Mermaid and undersea themed spot art (we pay $50 for spot illustrations)

Previously published mermaid and undersea illustrations and comics for us to reprint (we pay $25 – $50 licensing fee for interior and $100 – $150 for cover art licensing)

Non-fiction essay or article pitches for works up to 2,000 words (we pay $0.10 per word for non-fiction)

Reprints (we pay $0.01 per word for these with a minimum of $20 if the piece is shorter than 2,000 words)

How can I submit?

We will have a submission form for you when we open! If you are reading these guidelines and there is no link to a form, we are not open!

You will be able to attach your submission as a document on our submission form. If you have previously published art already displayed online that you would like us to consider, we’ll ask you to give us the link in a text document.
What are the themes you most want to see?

Everything should in some way relate to merfolk. We are loose about how you want to define that. We would love to see creative interpretations of the theme, and we’re also extremely interested in seeing work from writers of many backgrounds. Our staff includes BIPOC and queer people who are excited to explore diverse mermaid bodies, cultures, genders, abilities, religions, neurotypes, ethnicities, and more.

We are interested in happy and sad, light and dark, funny and serious. Most of all, we want to see what you most want to share.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Research and Resources
Forum thread: Real Life Publishing Opportunities

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) 'In Your Dreams: An instructional video on how to get the best sleep possible'
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Psychological Horror

Page Layout (Optional): More or less a traditional SCP article, though I plan to include a transcript of the tape and test results of those who viewed the tape.

Elevator Pitch: This SCP takes the form of a video tape. It is labelled 'In Your Dreams: an instructional video on how to get the best sleep possible' It starts out as a sleep instructional video before descending into madness, including subliminal messaging. The contents of the tape lead to massive psychological effects on whoever views the whole thing.

Central Narrative: The tape was discovered in the home of a suicide victim. The individual had no psychological issues prior to the viewing of the tape, which caught the attention of the SCP foundation. Attempts to find any info on the tape's origin has proven unsuccessful. However, the foundation has discovered multiple cases of homicides and suicides linked to this tape. All of the people who have viewed the tape and comply with all of its instructions suffer from insomnia, delusions, prone to self harm, sociopathic tendencies, and decreased empathy/compassion. Some extreme cases include incoherent rambling, and repeating the phrase "THERE ARE NO FACES."

In one incident, a copy of the tape was reportedly aired on TV in Mason County, Washington. Those who viewed the tape have received Class A amnesiacs, which have been proven successful with reversing the tapes effects

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There will be a disclaimer on the top stating that any staff who view the tape will be subject to Class A amnesiacs and an emergency psychological evaluation and that any unauthorized viewing of the tape will lead to termination, and any attempts at distributing the tape will lead to termination or reassignment to D-class.

Additional Notes: This was inspired by Local58's "real sleep". Honestly, the whole series is SCP material.

item.title: SCP Idea: The Muse
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Psychological Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Standard + Exploration logs

Elevator Pitch: From the perspective of the affected, a voice calls to them from inside their head, claiming to be their subconscious. It helps them along, allows them to remember things better, formulate ideas faster, etc. After a while, it will take the form of a humanoid hallucination, engaging in long conversations with the victim. The victim becomes more and more detached from reality, spiraling into ritual and insanity as the "muse" takes over more and more of their mind, eventually taking full control of their body.

Central Narrative: A small foundation site collapses as the head researcher comes under the affect of the Muse.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The reveal of the muse not being a figment of the victim's mind but rather an independent entity.

Additional Notes: I think this could either turn out very good and interesting or very cliché.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello Verillion! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey. It's nice to see the off-site fanbase make their way onto the official site for this little project. I can very much see why made-up scenarios keep you awake at night - after all, this site is all about it, isn't it? I really can't wait to see what kinds of writings you'll put on the site for us to enjoy!

Without further ado, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: Parasitic Amoeba
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX Is a species of omnivorous amoeba that travel extremely fast throughout liquids and can terminate any organism in seconds.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX-1 usually appears to those who have a small paycheck and have ease of access to a large container for water. Then SCP-XXXX-1 will dump a colony of SCP-XXXX into said container when the owner is near it. After dumping the colony the owner of the container will be frozen in place while SCP-XXXX walks towards and eventually into them, tell them to take care of the colony and then de-manifest.

Attention Grabber: I feel like there are a lot of SCPs that are either monstrous, cute or funny. But not all SCPs have to be that way. Another thing is that one thing goes through my head every time I hear of a K-Class end of the world scenario, that the world can be ended by something as big as a meteor or something as small as a micro-organism. I feel like there aren't enough small organisms in foundation custody that are capable of causing such an event.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea "Thunder"
item.content:encoded:
This is one of those weird ones: It's a great idea, but it's more of a cute one than anything else. You're going to need to show that the dog actually has an effect on its environment for it to be taken seriously; basically, you need to show that the dog is real despite being invisible.

I would, however, suggest you forego the vet report. To really have fun with SCP you need to do an interesting balancing act: You need to create doubt that the dog exists even as you need to show that it exists. This means that you need to show that the dog exists while at the same foregoing forensic evidence that it exists. So responding to barking before someone knocks on the door is cool, but a vet report not so much. Showing that a pair of slippers has been retrieved without him getting up is cool, but having film that the slippers are floating through the air not so much.

If you can hit that balance and create that doubt while not dispelling it either way you should be able to create a great SCP.

Forum thread: SCP-5083

Some day "I can fix this" will be uttered by a character undergoing a crisis, and they will be able to fix whatever this is. Today is not that day.

Very well done, overall. Compelling action, good call-backs, oodles of character development, and some interesting turns that, while not out of left field, still feel surprising. With halfway left for the rest of this cycle, I am very, very interested to see where it goes, in a way that I haven't been for a series in some time.

My one complaint is that the description of various characters is so distinctive that it's very obvious when you are cribbing from previous works, sometimes word for word (Medea has "shoulder-length brunette hair and faint blue eyes"; Jason has "mop of curly blond hair; Jeffery is "a middle-aged man with dark skin"; Anderson has "triangular grating that rapidly hissed with the passage of air" and "two small camera lenses that glowed with a faint green light"). They aren't bad descriptions, but it was a shame to be jerked out of the narrative several times by the realization that "hey, wait, didn't Conwell already say this?"

Still, an easy +1
